---
title: "code, data & model tests"
---

## what should be tested?

- a test checks an expected behaviour and fails when the observed result disagrees
- an assertion expresses that expectation inside a test; use explicit exceptions for required runtime checks outside tests
- passing tests provides evidence for the behaviours tested, while model suitability still needs evaluation for the intended task

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0"}

| test type | definition | useful example |
|---|---|---|
| unit | check one small component in isolation | a candidate gate rejects an invalid metric |
| integration | check components working together | api predictions match the saved pipeline |
| data contract | check schema and data-quality rules | reject a row with the wrong feature count |
| model quality | compare performance with predefined criteria | validation performance beats a baseline |
| regression | check that a change preserves an expected behaviour | fixed inputs still produce agreed predictions within a tolerance |
| smoke | run a small path to catch major failures | load the artifact and obtain one prediction |

:::

## tools and test vocabulary

- pytest is a python test runner; it discovers `test_` functions, executes assertions, and reports failures [pytest introduction](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/getting-started.html)
- a fixture provides reusable setup and cleanup, such as starting a test client; use it to keep tests independent [fixture guide](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/how-to/fixtures.html)
- fastapi’s `TestClient` sends requests to the application in-process, useful for checking endpoints without starting a network server [fastapi testing](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/testing/)
- a mock replaces a dependency during a test; use one to simulate a missing artifact or a failed training command
- a flaky test passes or fails inconsistently without a relevant change; investigate uncontrolled randomness, timing, or external dependencies

## test the serving exercise

- [download the complete automation exercise](../../examples/automation-demo.zip) into a fresh folder
- use python 3.12 and install `requirements-test.in`; it includes the app dependencies, pytest, and starlette’s optional client dependencies
- starlette is the underlying web framework supplying fastapi’s test client; the optional dependencies support its installed client version

```bash
python -m pip install -r requirements-test.in
python run_workflow.py --run-id run-001
python -m pytest -q
```

- the download contains `test_app.py`; this is one compact integration test, assuming the prepared `client` fixture

```python
def test_predictions_match_saved_pipeline(client):
    rows = [[0.0] * 10, [1.0] * 10]
    response = client.post("/predict", json={"rows": rows})
    assert response.status_code == 200
    model = joblib.load("artifacts/run-001/pipeline.joblib")
    expected = model.predict_proba(rows)[:, 1]
    np.testing.assert_allclose(response.json()["probabilities"], expected)
```

- numpy’s `assert_allclose` compares numeric results within a tolerance, useful for floating-point predictions
- the full tests also reject malformed inputs, check missing-artifact startup, and confirm a failed workflow does not become a candidate
- fixed examples catch regressions; use representative evaluation data and subgroup analysis to assess prediction quality beyond these examples
